title: Auction Disposition Expense Allowance in Kestrel Pre-Owned Retail Deficiency Quotes
content:
The auction's net proceeds, the gross sale price less its sale expenses, stay applied to principal as posted. In a deficiency quote on a Kestrel Pre-Owned Retail Installment Sale Contract, the auction's disposition expenses are allowed only up to a share of the gross sale price, and the part of those expenses above that share is credited against the deficiency figure. The credit is the expenses less the share times the gross sale price, never below zero.

The auction sale read is the most recent auction sale record on the contract; where two share a date, the first one listed is read. Its gross sale price and its sale expenses are used.

| How the vehicle came back, and the gross sale price | Share of the gross sale price allowed for expenses | Credit |
|---|---|---|
| Voluntary surrender | 6 percent (the voluntary-surrender expense share) | expenses less 6 percent of the gross sale price, never below zero |
| Involuntary recovery, gross sale price below $15000.00 (the low-value sale limit) | 10 percent (the low-value expense share) | expenses less 10 percent of the gross sale price, never below zero |
| Involuntary recovery, gross sale price of $15000.00 or more | the expenses stand as the auction deducted them | nothing is credited |

### Worked cases (hypothetical auction figures)

| Recovery | Gross sale price | Sale expenses | Allowed share | Credit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Involuntary | $9000.00 | $1400.00 | 10 percent, $900.00 | $500.00 |
| Voluntary surrender | $9000.00 | $1400.00 | 6 percent, $540.00 | $860.00 |
| Involuntary | $9000.00 | $700.00 | 10 percent, $900.00 | $0.00 — never below zero |
| Involuntary | $15000.00 | $2500.00 | — | nothing; $15000.00 is not below the limit |
